rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah proves that the Book is guidance; its highest guidance is faith in the unseen, centered on resurrection and the Hereafter, and the Cow story makes resurrection especially evident.
rows.anchor: مقصودها إقامة الدليل على أن الكتاب هدى ليتبع يفي كل ما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Cow story is a better title than Abraham's story because it concerns ordinary human beings and an apparently weak cause of revival, making divine power clearer; it is linked to other revivals among Israel's children.
rows.anchor: وكانت بذلك أحق من قصة إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنها في نوع البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is also called al-Zahra because it illuminates guidance and sufficiency in both worlds and brings brightness to believers' faces on the Day of Judgment; faith in the Hereafter is the highest completion after tawhid.
rows.anchor: وسميت الزهراء لإنارتها طريق الهداية والكفاية في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as making guidance manifest, extending mercy to all creation by showing the way, and granting special enabling to those He loves.
rows.anchor: الذي أفاض رحمته على سائر خلقه بعد الإيجاد ببيان الطريق

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says earlier scripture came through one door and one letter, while the Quran came through seven doors and seven letters: commands, prohibitions, lawful, forbidden, clear, ambiguous, and parables.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says the seven-letters report is unestablished: Abu Salama did not meet Ibn Masud and his son Salama is not a reliable proof.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر بن عبد البر

rows.speaker: أبو شامة
rows.claim: Abu Shama says al-Bayhaqi's mursal transmission is good; if the report is sound, its seven letters mean seven kinds of Quranic content, not permitted dialects.
rows.anchor: قال أبو شامة : وهكذا رواه البيهقي في كتاب المدخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author records versions from al-Tabarani, Ibn Abi Dawud, and al-Bayhaqi: the seven categories recur, while Abu Hurayra's report lists five aspects, omitting commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: ورواه البيهقي في فضل القرآن من الشعب عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali relates another seven-letters report through Ibn Umar and interprets the Quran as completing the earlier scriptures and gathering the ends of creation and religious order.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : زفي حديث آخر من طريق ابن عمر

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali divides the six shared letters into worldly law (lawful and forbidden), the Hereafter (command and prohibition), and religion (clear and ambiguous); the Quran completes what earlier books began.
rows.anchor: فأدنى تلك الحروف هو حرف إصلاح الدنيا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The seventh, unique letter is praise and the parable, given to Muhammad as a unifying gift; it appears through his heart, recitation, and person, beyond the six letters reached through intermediaries.
rows.anchor: ويختص القرآن بالحرف السابع الجامع مبين المثل الأعلى ومظهر اللمثول الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the Prophet's prayer asking that religion, worldly livelihood, and the Hereafter each be set right, and the report that he was sent to perfect noble character.
rows.anchor: اللهم أصلح لي ديني الذي هو عصمة أمري

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali maps al-Fatiha's verses to the seven letters: praise, lawful and forbidden, command and prohibition, clear and ambiguous, then the corresponding petitions; its opening gathers all seven.
rows.anchor: فالآية الأولى تشتمل على حرف الحمد السابع

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: He offers two readings of the merciful names: universal mercy permits created benefits while specific mercy protects from harm; he says the nearer reading is general lordly beneficence and a special divine mercy directed to felicity.
rows.anchor: وأما الرحيمية فطهرتهم من مضار أبدانهم ورجاسة نفوسهم ومجهلة قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran opens with the ambiguous sixth letter to teach belief in what is unseen and humble submission, which prepares the reader to follow what is clear; the Fatiha already opens with the gifted seventh letter.
rows.anchor: ابتدئ القرآن بالحرف السادس المعجوز عنه وهو حرف المتشابه

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr sees the disjointed openings as a challenge: the Quran uses one half of the alphabet, leaving the other half for opponents to compose a rival; al-Zarkashi also cites Abu Bakr and Ali on the letters' hidden status.
rows.anchor: نقل ذلك الزركشي في البرهان عن القاضي أبي بكر

rows.speaker: ابن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says alif-lam-mim gathers the throat, tongue, and lips in sequence, signaling creation, worldly life and its laws, and resurrection; surahs with these openings address all three.
rows.anchor: وأبدى الإمام شمس الدين ابن فقيم الجوزيه الدمشقي الحنبلي

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali assigns alif to the highest standing, mim to the highest manifestation including Muhammad, and lam to the connection between divine hiddenness and manifestation, with corresponding created examples.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي في تفسيره : ' الف '

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali treats the opening letters as comprehensive roots of God's speech preserved in the Quran as signs of its heavenly source; their completeness suits the completed cosmos at Muhammad's time.
rows.anchor: فهي في الكنب العلوية الملكوتية المترتبة في الجمع والتفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition from al-Fatiha's plea for the straight path to al-Baqara identifies that guidance with this Book, then describes the guided and rejected groups to teach the path to follow and the path to avoid.
rows.anchor: وأما منسبة ما بعد ذلك للفاتحة فهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the surah's central purpose is to establish the Book's true meaning and form: it exposes hypocrisy, calls people to worship, proves its inimitability, then teaches law and debates the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: مقصود هذه السورة وصف الكتاب فقط وما عدا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to worship is followed by creation as proof that God deserves worship; the warning against partners follows because the creation evidence establishes that He has no partner in worship or creation.
rows.anchor: إلى آخره بوصف هو دليل استحقاقه للعبادة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The address rises from God's lordship to divinity because primordial recognition of the One is rooted in human nature; association enters at the level of worship, so 'there is no deity but He' removes that implication.
rows.anchor: فكان هذا أوسط الدعوة بالاجتماع في وحدة الإلهية وفي إضافة اسم الإله إليهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The merciful names make the unseen divine reality recognizable through universal mercy and special favor; with 3:1-4 they encompass mercy and the counterpoint of might and vengeance.
rows.anchor: فكان في مجموع هذه الآية أعظمية من غيب الإلهية إلى تمام اختصاص الرحيمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in 2:164 expand the preceding evidence to prove God's knowledge and power and, especially, exclusive divinity, since apparent proximate causes do not act independently.
rows.anchor: نصب الأدلة على ذلك في هذه الآية الثالثة بأبسط مما في الآية الثانية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The final community was spared the demand for extraordinary signs because earlier peoples who denied them were punished; the Prophet's sign is revelation, so this community is invited to learn through created evidence instead.
rows.anchor: ولما كان من سنة الله أن من دعاه إليه وإلى رسله بشاهد خرق عادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical ellipsis mentions creation first as evidence for omitting it second, then mentions variation second as evidence for omitting it first.
rows.anchor: ذكر الخلق أولا دليلا على حذفه ثانيا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The ordered union of opposites, such as fire with water and air with earth, cannot be produced by creatures; their combination in bodies and organs shows the one God whose effects are visible and whose reality reason can recognize.
rows.anchor: والحق سبحانه وتعالى أقام للخلق والموجودات والموالد آحادا مجتمعة قد قهر فيها متنافرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Large ships are distinguished from small boats; their sailing is figuratively attributed to them although only God makes them move, rejecting philosophers' belief in the independent agency of stars.
rows.anchor: أسند الجري إليها ومن المعلوم أنه لا جري لها حقيقة ولا فعل بوجه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The ships distribute useful goods among peoples and directions; the general phrase 'what benefits people' includes every useful cargo and points to human cooperation.
rows.anchor: فما حملت جارية شيئا ينتفع به إلا قد تضمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain from the sky revives the barren earth after its lack of growth, and the water disperses every kind of self-moving creature across it.
rows.anchor: بما ينبت منها ولما كان الإحياء يستغرق الزمن

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says God's name is made manifest with the earth where life is visible, while his name is shown where it is hidden from people; water's arrival draws worship toward the God above.
rows.anchor: وأظهر الاسم مع الأرض لظهوره في الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet tested a slave woman's faith by asking where God is; she answered 'in heaven,' and he told her owner to free her.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام للأمة : ( أين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wind changes direction under divine governance, while clouds are suspended between heaven and earth despite their weight and contrary to the tendencies of dense and subtle matter.
rows.anchor: وهو المتراكم في جهة العلو من جوهر ما بين الماء والهواء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The visible elements also signify inner realities: rain revives hearts with knowledge, and winds and clouds portray the changes between a servant's outward and inward life under God's rule.
rows.anchor: ويكون ما أنزل من الماء لإحياء الأرض وخلق الحيوان آية ما ينزل من نور علمه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The 'people' who understand are those mature in strong reflection, and reason is a divine light by which they read the signs in creation and scripture.
rows.anchor: وذكر تعالى العقل الذي هو نور من نوره هدى لمن أقامه من حد تردد حال الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variations show a freely acting, powerful creator who can resurrect the dead and is one without rival; they also encompass the essential beliefs about God's existence, unity, transcendence, creation, and governance.
rows.anchor: فيعلمون أن مصرف هذه الأمور على هذه الكيفيات المختلفة والوجوه المحكمة فاعل مختار

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says that the divine names established by scripture and scholarly agreement are distributed among the five essential beliefs, and a name may belong to more than one category.
rows.anchor: قال البيهقي : كان أسماء الله سبحانه وتعالى جده التي ورد بها الكتاب والسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proofs are multiplied because capacities differ: sensory knowledge of the visible world is open to everyone, while the unseen is grasped by people of sound intellect; creation offers varied routes proportionate to each person's capacity except for sealed hearts.
rows.anchor: العالم وهو الممكنات الموجودة وهي جملة ما سواه الدالة على وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recognizing God's nearness and recalling the sweetness of addressing Him, the fasting believers longed for ease; the verse answers their implied request concerning intimacy and eating at night.
rows.anchor: فتذكروا لذيذ مخاطبته فيما قبل فاشتاقوا إليها وكان قد يسر لهم أمر الصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nighttime intercourse is permitted for the whole fasting night; rafath means sexual speech or intercourse, and the phrase 'to your wives' excludes other men's wives. The clothing metaphor either describes intimacy or spouses' mutual need.
rows.anchor: فأشعر ذلك بأنه كان حراما

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Bara reports that during Ramadan people initially avoided intercourse with their wives throughout the month, then some betrayed themselves before the permission was revealed.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري في التفسير عن البراء رضي الله تعالى عنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fasting man who slept before eating could not eat until the next night; Sirma b. Qays slept, fainted before midday, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وإن صرمة بن قيس الأنصاري رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says God pardoned violations caused by human disposition, then eased the law to fit this community's nature; reports of one Emigrant and one Ansari show the mercy reached both groups.
rows.anchor: وكانت هذه الواقعة لرجل من المهاجرين ورجل من الأنصار ليجتمع اليمن في الطائفتين

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha told the Prophet that his Lord hastened to satisfy his desire, illustrating the special easing granted to the community through him.
rows.anchor: كما قالت عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The Prophet told Ali to ask God to make truth turn with him; the author also says wise leaders adapt commands to people's dispositions, like directing the brave to fight and restraining the coward.
rows.anchor: وكما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام لعلي رضي الله تعالى عنه : ( اللهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet considered forbidding ghila, then refrained after learning that Persians and Romans practiced it without harm to their children; law should account for different human natures.
rows.anchor: لقد هممت أن أنهى عن الغيلة حتى سمعت أن فارس والروم يصنعون ذلك

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Forgiveness erases the trace of wrongdoing and hints that purification such as expiation might otherwise have been due; Ramadan fasting elevates the community beyond earlier separated days and nights.
rows.anchor: أي بمحو أثر الذنب إشعار بما كان يستحق ذلك من تطهر

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Nighttime intercourse becomes obedience to God's command rather than mere appetite; 'what God prescribed' may mean offspring or a lawful place for sex, and some scholars favored marriage for the fasting person at night.
rows.anchor: فصار نكاحهم ائتمارا بحكم الله لا إجابة طبع ولا غرض نفس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet would break his fast with fresh dates, then dates, and if neither was available, sips of water; the author sees the order as following human appetite and need.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يفطر على رطبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making dawn's appearance the endpoint of permitted food and sex requires watching for dawn and supports intending the fast before it; intercourse continuing to dawn shows that ritual bathing may wait until daytime.
rows.anchor: فإن في جعل تبين الفجر غاية لحل المفطرات إيجابا لمراقبته للكف عنها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The form yatabayyana suggests that the observer must exert effort to discern dawn; 'for you' indicates that legal judgments follow what is outwardly accessible and within human capacity.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : بصيغة يتفعل وهو حيث يتكلف الناظر نظره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The black thread is explained as the darkness at the end of night, likened to a black line beside the white dawn thread.
rows.anchor: ظلمة آخر الليل , شبها بخطين أبيض وأسود

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says 'from dawn' clarifies the metaphor by identifying its referent as a simile; Adi b. Hatim had misunderstood the image literally, so the added explanation prevents ambiguity.
rows.anchor: وقد كان أنزل هذا المثل دون بيان ممثوله حتى أخذ أعرابي ينظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the verse was not left ambiguous or unexplained until the time of need, since the Prophet did not blame Adi for his misunderstanding; mentioning dawn instead of night is eloquent reliance on what is understood.
rows.anchor: فلم تكن الآية مجملة ولا تأخر البيان عن وقت الحاجة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: In his legal theory, al-Harali allows an initially general or ambiguous address whose binding clarification comes later; it still benefits gradual revelation and recitation, although the author elsewhere denies ambiguity here.
rows.anchor: والخطاب بالإجمال ممكن الوقوع وليس يلزم العمل به

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali finds an Arabic rhetorical pattern in the third phrase returning semantically to the first while joining grammatically to the second, preserving the omitted night through implication.
rows.anchor: لأن العرب يردون الثالث إلى الأول لا إلى الثاني ليتعلق بالأول في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the fast until night makes abstention obligatory after dawn and signals the temporal gap between the permitted night and fasting day; some scholars inferred that i'tikaf begins before sunset.
rows.anchor: وأوضح دليل على إيجاب التبييت أمره بالإتمام

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says daytime is for work and interaction, while night is rest and a time of divine manifestation; night eating is like being fed by God and does not negate the fast's spiritual reality.
rows.anchor: ولأن الليل سبات ووقت توف وانطماس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercourse is forbidden throughout i'tikaf wherever the worshipper is; specifying mosques either honors the setting or, preferably, defines ritual i'tikaf as devotional confinement there. Combining i'tikaf and fasting strengthens the prohibition.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أنه سبحانه وتعالى سوى بين حال الصوم حال الاعتكاف في المنع من الجماع

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines complete fasting as restraint from ordinary transactions, desires, and retaliation, with speech and conduct guarded; its inward reality matters more than abstaining from food alone.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وإنما كان العاكف في المسجد مكملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites reports that Ramadan plus six days of Shawwal, or three days each month, equals fasting a lifetime; some Companions could say they were fasting in divine favor while eating as God's guests.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( من صام رمضان وأبعه بسبت من شوال فكأنما صام الدهر
